title: Spring Framework 7.0: ReactorClientHttpRequestFactory.setConnectTimeout(Duration) fails with 'Timeout must be a non-negative value' for timeouts above about 24.8 days
errorSample:
Caused by: java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Timeout must be a non-negative value
	at org.springframework.util.Assert.isTrue(Assert.java:117) ~[spring-core-7.0.9.jar:7.0.9]
	at org.springframework.http.client.ReactorClientHttpRequestFactory.setConnectTimeout(ReactorClientHttpRequestFactory.java:156) ~[spring-web-7.0.9.jar:7.0.9]
	at org.springframework.http.client.ReactorClientHttpRequestFactory.setConnectTimeout(ReactorClientHttpRequestFactory.java:169) ~[spring-web-7.0.9.jar:7.0.9]
	at task.PartnerApiConfig.partnerRestClient(Application.kt:30) ~[main/:na]

appliesTo.versions: 7.0.x (7.0.9 in Spring Boot 4.0.8); fixed in 7.1.0-RC1, not backported to 7.0.x

sources.license: Facts summarized from a public GitHub issue/PR; short error excerpt quoted.

symptom: Creating a RestClient with ReactorClientHttpRequestFactory fails with IllegalArgumentException: Timeout must be a non-negative value when the configured connect timeout is longer than about 25 days (30d fails, 7d works). With SimpleClientHttpRequestFactory the same value is silently ignored or turns into a wrong short timeout.
cause: setConnectTimeout(Duration) narrows duration.toMillis() to int with a plain cast. Above Integer.MAX_VALUE milliseconds (about 24.8 days) the value overflows, 30 days becomes negative, and the int overload's non-negative assertion fails. Values such as 50 days wrap to an unrelated positive number.
fixSummary: Clamp the duration in application code before passing it, for example setConnectTimeout(minOf(timeout, Duration.ofMillis(Int.MAX_VALUE.toLong()))), which keeps the setting effectively unbounded and leaves ReactorClientHttpRequestFactory in use. Fixed in Framework 7.1.0-RC1 only.
